summary.title: Welcome to Linux command line for you and me!
summary.one_liner: A broad, sectioned Linux command-line guide (the "lym" book) covering shell basics, file handling, vim, curl, users and processes, systemd services, package management, networking, and firewalls.
takeaways: Learn everyday shell commands such as ls, cd, cp, mkdir, rm, find-style file handling, and output redirection
Use vim basics, curl for HTTP requests and headers, and bash history tricks
Understand users, groups, file permissions, processes, signals, and /proc
Manage systemd services and read logs with journalctl; harden services with systemd options
Work with dnf and apt packages, basic networking tools (ip, dig, ssh), and iptables or nftables firewalls
summary.summary: This is an online book/tutorial structured as a table of contents of short topic sections, aimed at people learning the Linux command line. The page text shown is the index only, so the depth of each section is not visible here. It covers shell and file basics, vim, curl, users and processes, systemd and journalctl, package managers dnf and apt, networking tools, ssh, and firewalls with iptables and nftables. It is edited by Jason Braganza, with contributions from Kushal Das.
